text: {"status":"contradicted","evidence_ids":["ev-4eeac5d8d8f2fdb9fe36a5b5","ev-f0e158f3ccaf6a5ac4c89ea6","ev-410a80498fe825072db7b101"],"request_dft":false,"proposed_test_ids":[],"rationale":"No peers have spoken yet, so there is nothing to support or dispute. The claim concerns the archived records. The unit-cell record gives -4.94416 eV/atom and the 3x3 supercell record gives -3.92666 eV/atom. Both are converged DFT relaxations with the same method signature (VASP 6.6.0, PBE, ENCUT 520, same POTCAR, same 20 Å vacuum). Both reached the required ionic accuracy, with residual forces of 0.0039 and 0.0004 eV/Å. The in-plane area per atom is identical at 3.626 Å^2. The comparison record gives |ΔE| = 1.0175 eV/atom, about 100 times the 0.01 eV/atom threshold. I re-derived this from the totals: -141.3598894/36 and -19.77664371/4 reproduce the per-atom values and the 1.0175 difference. The k-mesh difference (8x11x1 vs 3x4x1) corresponds to roughly the same sampling density and cannot plausibly produce a 1 eV/atom shift. So, as archived, the two records do not describe the same pristine sheet at the stated tolerance. The claim is contradicted. A shift this large is physically suspect for the same sheet. It points to a defective record, such as a different structure or inconsistent POTCAR or electron count in one calculation. That is a diagnosis of why the archive is inconsistent, not a way to rescue the claim. The rebuild-and-relax test could explain the cause, but it is not needed to decide this claim. Assumption: the comparison arithmetic is correct. I checked it and it is. Falsification of my verdict would require showing that one OUTCAR was mis-parsed, in which case the records would be inadmissible and the claim would become unresolved."}
